tip: A feminine singular noun soft-mutates a following adjective: after gath, du becomes ddu.
Welsh builds the passive with cael ei plus the verb-noun: cael ei hadrodd means it is being told.
The word ei meaning his soft-mutates what follows: after ei, bai becomes fai.
The -odd ending marks the past tense for he, she or it: Cyrhaeddodd means arrived.
Before an adjective the linking yn soft-mutates it: yn fyr comes from byr.
Pe bawn i sets up an unreal, hypothetical if: pe bawn i wedi gwybod means if I had known.
A feminine singular noun soft-mutates after y: dinas becomes y ddinas.
Am soft-mutates the word after it: cerdd becomes gerdd in am gerdd.
Welsh shows possession by placing nouns side by side: dyfodol yr iaith means the language's future.
The -wch ending gives a command to more than one person, or a polite one: Neidiwch means jump.
The -wyd ending marks an impersonal past passive: Enillwyd means was won.
Ar ôl plus a verb-noun means after doing something: ar ôl cwblhau means after completing.
Prif comes before its noun and soft-mutates it: canfyddiadau becomes prif ganfyddiadau.
Yn meaning in triggers nasal mutation and itself becomes ym: pob turns into ym mhob.
The word â (with) triggers aspirate mutation: canfyddiadau becomes â chanfyddiadau.
The ending -wraig marks a female doer: sgriptiwraig means a woman scriptwriter.
O (of) soft-mutates the word after it: tasgau becomes o dasgau.
